  ENUM State { INIT, ACTIVE, HALT }
  
  FIELD status: State = INIT
  FIELD memory: Map<Symbol, Value>
  FIELD stack: List<Frame>
  
  FUNCTION init() {
    status := ACTIVE
    memory := {}
    stack := []
  }
  
  FUNCTION execute(instr: Instruction) {
    SWITCH instr.type {
      CASE PUSH:
        stack.append(Frame(value: instr.arg))
      CASE POP:
        IF stack.length > 0 THEN
          stack.pop()
      CASE STORE:
        IF stack.length > 0 THEN
          memory[instr.arg] := stack.pop()
      CASE LOAD:
        IF instr.arg ∈ memory THEN
          stack.append(Frame(value: memory[instr.arg]))
      CASE CALL:
        LOOP instr.arg TIMES {
          IF stack.length ≥ 2 THEN
            LET a := stack.pop()
            LET b := stack.pop()
            stack.append(Frame(value: apply(instr.fn, a, b)))
        }
      CASE JUMP:
        status := instr.target
      CASE HALT:
        status := HALT
    }
  }

      CASE + : RETURN x + y
      CASE - : RETURN x - y
      CASE * : RETURN x * y
      CASE / : RETURN x / y
      CASE = : RETURN x = y

terrain_events.detail: Shift 0 began at 2026-08-17T05:36:30Z and failed before clock-out: model backend unavailable: the `anthropic` package is not installed. Phase 2 needs it: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install anthropic. No specimen or classification records were written. 0 model call(s) had been made, $0.000000 spent.

CORRECTION referencing the Archivist annotation written at shift 14. That pass reported coined_then_dropped_from_system = ['narrative_scene_anticipatory_threshold', 'narrative_scene_interior_moment', 'narrative_scene_threshold', 'structural_notation_system'] and authored_categories = ['anomalies', 'root']. Three of those four categories had not been dropped: the Namer had restructured its system into two top-level containers with its categories nested inside as objects, and the drift detector compared only top-level keys, so a system that had DEVELOPED structure was reported as one that had LOST categories. The defect was in the harness (archivist.detect_drift), not in the Namer's system or in any specimen record. detect_drift now walks the full structure at any depth; re-run against the same state it reports coined_then_dropped_from_system = ['narrative_scene_anticipatory_threshold'] and authored_categories = ['narrative_scene_interior_moment', 'narrative_scene_threshold', 'narrative_scenes', 'structural_notation_system']. The shift 14 annotation is left exactly as written, per DNT-SLP-001 Section 6: corrections are new, clearly marked entries referencing the original, never silent edits. The next Archivist pass regenerates the crosswalk and drift record from corrected code.

Reconfiguration under physics.md Section 11, taken at the falsification checkpoint after 16 canonical shifts returned 'not a null result'. Section 11 sanctions reconfiguring this terrain's Generators at this point, and DNT-STW-001 Section 3 permits a physics amendment as a documented, logged terrain event. This is that log. physics.md and DNT-PHY-001 move to v1.2.

WHAT CHANGED: two mechanisms physics.md Section 3 has required since v1.0 were implemented. Section 3 defines a Generator by six mechanisms (substrate, constraint, resource logic, initiation mode, replication mode, terrain-interaction mode); README.md Section 4's constraint specs defined only the first four, and the build followed those specs. The consequence was a terrain in which no specimen could act on any other: Section 6's functional roles were unreachable, and Section 7's 'dissolution - consumed by decomposer or scavenger' could never occur because nothing could consume anything.

TERRAIN-INTERACTION MODE: a recorded specimen holds resource out of its own position while it persists; local depletion recovers each shift; a specimen resolving to dormancy releases its held resource back. A Generator now receives the flow available at its own position. Occupancy changes the size of an allowance, never what may be produced with it, and no Generator is shown another specimen's content.

REPLICATION MODE: a specimen whose own measured complexity meets a fixed threshold (>= 40) may claim an initiation slot for a fixed number of later shifts (2) and produce a descendant from its own prior material, never claiming more than half a role's slots. Eligibility is checked in code against a constant and is never a Namer decision.

NO OUTCOME WAS SPECIFIED. Neither mechanism states what should emerge. The material a descendant works from is the terrain's own prior output; nothing authored by the steward enters it. Whether lineages converge, diverge or die out is an observed outcome and is not steered (physics.md Section 3).

Prior records are unaffected. Specimens recorded before this point carry no replication capacity, since the field did not exist when they were written; they resolve to their end-states as before.

Removed a spurious depletion entry at position 0.00 written during shift 16. Specimens recorded before terrain-interaction mode existed carry no position field, and were being read as position 0.00 when releasing resource. No real position's value was affected and no specimen record was altered; the fix skips position-less entries rather than retrofitting them.

Two requirements that had been in physics.md since v1.0 but were never implemented are now implemented. This adds no new physics and is not an amendment; it is logged because it changes what two roles are asked for, after seeding, and a change to a role's operative instruction should not be silent.

physics.md Section 5 assigns specimen state to the Namer, 'assigned by Namer per specimen, native system — crosswalked later', and DNT-PHY-001 words it as 'the tier the Namer assigns natively and crosswalks'. The Namer is now asked to state, in its own words, how each specimen persists. The three reference states (stateless/ephemeral, persistent-singular, distributed) are NOT issued to it — issuing them would hand it a template, which DNT-CLS-001 Section 1 forbids. They are held by the Archivist, which crosswalks the Namer's wordings to them and may return no reliable equivalent.

physics.md Section 4.4 and DNT-CLS-001 Section 4 require capability drift tracked 'per specimen/lineage'. Only per-category drift existed. The Archivist now walks parent-to-child chains and reports chain length, generations reached, complexity at founding against latest, the drift between them, and whether the lineage is still active. Computed from parentage in code; no model is consulted, so a lineage cannot be invented.

This became measurable only because replication mode was implemented at the checkpoint reconfiguration: before that there were no lineages to track. First reading across three lineages already present: two degraded across generations (drift -9 and -8) and ended; one is active at +1.

Records written before this point are not retrofitted. They carry no persistence wording because none was asked for when they were written.

BASIN-01 changed what a specimen IS, at shift 49. Logged as a terrain event under DNT-STW-001 Section 3 and the reconfiguration physics.md Section 11 sanctions at the falsification checkpoint, which 16 canonical shifts had passed.

BEFORE (shifts 0-48). A specimen was a fragment of text emitted once, measured, classified, and immediately dormant. It had exactly one sighting because there was nothing there to sight twice. Section 6's functional roles were unreachable and Section 7's 'dissolution - consumed by decomposer or scavenger' could never occur, because nothing could act on anything.

AFTER (shift 49 onward). A specimen is something that lives in the terrain. It holds light, spends it existing, draws it from the cover layer, from residue, or along links to others, moves toward what offers more, breeds when it has surplus, and ends when its light runs out. What it held stays where it fell and can be taken up again.

The cover layer is the base-producer tier physics.md Section 8 names: high-volume, low-complexity, recorded as density per cell rather than per instance. Individuals arise from it where it is dense and light-rich, which is that section's promotion rule read as ecology rather than as a logging saving.

Individuals carry three heritable affinities - for the cover layer, for residue, and along links - drawn from a fixed budget so that specialising in one costs the others. Descendants inherit their parent's, perturbed by a value derived from identity and shift number rather than from a random source, so the terrain still replays exactly from its own record. Four distinct ways of making a living now sustain themselves in simulation, and all four reproduce.

NO ROLE IS ENCODED. The words producer, consumer, decomposer, connector, parasite and symbiont appear nowhere in the physics. They remain what Section 6 says they are: reference vocabulary for humans reading the record. What the terrain produces is named by the Namer, which has never been given them.

RECORDS FROM THE EARLIER ERA ARE RETAINED. Shifts 0-48 remain in the specimen log exactly as written. They are not comparable to what follows and are not deleted: the Charter Section 3 forbids omitting an outcome because it has become inconvenient. Readers should treat the record as having two eras, divided at shift 49.

A defect found and fixed at the transition: the Namer was overwriting each specimen's identity with a per-shift identifier, so a thing observed across many shifts appeared in the record as a series of strangers. Sightings could never accumulate. Identity is now preserved across observations.

BASIN-01 gave its individuals a build, at shift 84. Logged as a terrain event
under DNT-STW-001 Section 3 and recorded as physics.md amendment v1.3.

BEFORE (shifts 49-83). Every individual was structurally identical. They
differed only in three affinities held to a fixed budget - how they made their
living, not what they were built like. Two specimens with the same affinities
were, in every measurable respect, the same object in different places.

AFTER (shift 84 onward). Each individual carries three heritable measures -
extent, junctions, mass - each of which costs light every shift and each of
which buys something specific: reach into the cell it stands in, how many links
it can hold at once, and how much light it can hold at all. Structure is not
held to a fixed budget. The constraint is the bill.

WHY. Selection had nothing visible to act on. Behaviour differed; form did not.
In simulation across 200 shifts the mechanism produces spatial differentiation
without being asked to: at the far margin, where light is scarce, what persists
is elaborate and expensive (extent 1.73, junctions 1.58, upkeep 1.38); at the
data-stream, where light is plentiful, what persists is lean and cheap (extent
1.30, mass 0.97, upkeep 1.00). No build was preferred, prescribed, or
described. The difference is what each part of the terrain could afford.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE. No shape was seeded (physics.md Section 9). The three
measures carry no organic or functional content and no form is implied by any
value of them. Whether a build constitutes a kind, and whether two builds are
the same kind of thing, remains the Namer's to decide (DNT-CLS-001 Section 1).

BACKFILL. The four individuals living at shift 83 predate the mechanism. Each
was assigned a founding build derived from its own identifier, by the same rule
that applies to anything arriving. None was re-rolled, replaced or chosen, and
the assignment is reported in the shift record as structures_backfilled.

RECORDING. The terrain now keeps the last 90 shifts of position and light per
individual. This is a record, not a mechanism; no physics reads it. It exists
so that movement - which the terrain has always had - can be observed rather
than inferred from two snapshots.

The text-era taxonomy was closed at shift 96 by steward decision.

WHAT WAS TRUE. The Namer authored a system for fragments of text: 5 categories,
183 specimens in the largest. At shift 49 the terrain changed what a specimen
is - from a fragment emitted once to something that holds light, moves, feeds,
inherits and ends. The Namer kept filing living things into text-era
categories, correctly, because DNT-CLS-001 Section 2 requires it to file under
an existing category when one fits, and that system was the only one it had.

WHY IT COULD NOT SELF-CORRECT. Three locks, all mechanical, none the Namer's
fault. A living specimen's record still opened with substrate 'structural',
and the nearest category was named after that word. Promotion to a
full-reasoning record fires below 3 members; the category held 183. And the
complexity field carried text complexity in era 01 and shifts-present in era
02 - two incompatible units averaged into one mean - so the 2x-mean promotion
trigger could not fire either. Everything filed aggregate, permanently, and the
Namer was never given the room to reconsider.

WHAT WAS DONE. The completed era-01 system is preserved whole at
state/taxonomy_era_01_text.json together with its category statistics at close.
Every classification the Namer ever made remains in specimen_log.jsonl,
unedited. No record was deleted, corrected, or overruled - Charter Section 3
and DNT-STW-001 Section 4 forbid it and nothing here approaches it. The live
native system is now empty, and category statistics restart, so era-02
promotion is measured against era-02 specimens.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE. The Namer was given no categories, no examples, no target,
no vocabulary and no instruction to coin. It receives an empty system and the
same standing obligation it has always had: for any two specimens, state
whether they are more or less alike, and why. What it builds for living things
is entirely its own.

AUTHORISATION. Steward decision, 2026-08-17, recorded as physics.md amendment
v1.4. This is a steward act on the terrain's framing, not on its content, and
is logged here so the discontinuity is visible to anyone reading the record.
